page_title: JuiceMount: open-source Suite, Shade & LucidLink alternative

summary.name: JuiceMount
summary.one_liner: An open-source (Apache-2.0) macOS app that mounts a NAS as a real drive in Finder, storing files as 4 MB blocks for fast partial reads and editing video off the NAS.
use_cases: editing large video files stored on a NAS
sharing a project volume with a small post team
scrubbing footage without copying whole files
working offline on a laptop with pinned projects
fast filename search across large NAS projects
replacing paid storage SaaS for media collaboration
summary.what_it_does: JuiceMount mounts a NAS volume at /Volumes/JuiceMount so it appears in Finder like a local drive, with the same paths for every teammate who mounts it. Files are stored on the NAS as 4 MB blocks (JuiceFS format), so reading a few seconds of a large clip only fetches the blocks touched, and a local SSD cache keeps recently used blocks. It provides a filename search window (⌘⇧F) backed by a local SQLite index on the Mac, with Quick Look and drag-into-timeline support. A menu bar app controls the server, pinning projects for offline use, syncing, and offline mode.
notable: Stores files as 4 MB blocks so only the needed parts of large video files move over the network
Local SQLite filename index for search in about 29 ms without querying the NAS
Real mounted volume with stable paths so Premiere and Resolve don't need relinking
Apache-2.0 licensed software that runs on hardware the user already owns
caveats: Performance figures (about 7 Gbit/s on 10 GbE) are the author's own measurements on one Apple-Silicon Mac and TrueNAS rig, not independent benchmarks
TrueNAS SCALE is described as the production-tested install path; other NAS platforms are listed as runnable via Docker
Requires macOS 14 or later and a NAS or Docker-capable Linux box the user must provide
